# Buyer Quirk Sheet: Transnet SOC Ltd (incl. Transnet National Ports Authority)

- **Buyer:** Transnet SOC Ltd [Registration Number 1990/000900/30] and its Operating Divisions — Transnet National Ports Authority (TNPA), Transnet Port Terminals, Transnet Pipelines, Transnet Rail Infrastructure Manager, Transnet Property, Transnet Engineering
- **Kind:** National state-owned enterprise (SOE), Schedule 2 public entity
- **Packs sampled:** 10 — transnet-shore-assistance-rfq (TNPA/2026/07/1606/9023/RFQ), ocds-9t57fa-165125 (TPL/2026/07/0433/8067/RFP), ocds-9t57fa-164429 (TPT/2026/07/0889/9678/RFQ), ocds-9t57fa-165605 (WRAC-VAR-58045), ocds-9t57fa-164857 (TNPA Port of Durban lease notice), ocds-9t57fa-164264 (TNPA/2026/07/0004/114622/RFP), ocds-9t57fa-165699 (Contractor Environmental & Sustainability Specification Guidelines), ocds-9t57fa-165036 (TP/2026/07/0128/8221/RFP-CIDB), ocds-9t57fa-165033 (TNPA Floating Dry Dock Facility Operator Agreement / Section 56 TOA), ocds-9t57fa-165835 (TE/2026/08/3365/10069/RFQ)
- **Date:** 2026-08

---

## Submission channel & rules

Transnet is **electronic-only across every pack sampled** — there is no hard-copy/box channel and no dual-channel rule to reconcile. All bids go through the "Transnet e-Tender Submission Portal" / "Transnet Digital Procurement System (TDPS) eSupplier Portal" (https://esupplierportal.transnet.net/portal/ and https://transnetetenders.azurewebsites.net).

- Registration is per-company; a bidder must "log an intent to bid" and submit under its **own** registered profile, never through another company's profile, even a subsidiary/holding-company relationship (ocds-9t57fa-164264: *"Transnet will not accept a bid or will disqualify a bidder who submits a bid in the Transnet e-tender submission through another bidders'/Company's profile... No company shall submit a bid on behalf of another company regardless of the company being a subsidiary or holding company."*). Joint ventures may submit through any one JV party's profile (ocds-9t57fa-164264: *"In case of a Joint Venture, any of the parties/companies to the Joint Venture may use its registered profile to submit a bid on behalf of the Joint Venture."*).
- Uploads are capped at 30MB per file, multiple uploads permitted (transnet-shore-assistance-rfq: *"Bidders should ensure that electronic bid submissions are submitted at least a day before the closing date... Transnet will not be held liable for any challenges experienced by bidders as a result of their own technical challenges."*; same wording repeated verbatim in ocds-9t57fa-164264, ocds-9t57fa-164429, ocds-9t57fa-165605, ocds-9t57fa-165036).
- **No late submissions accepted under any circumstances** (ocds-9t57fa-164264: *"h) No late submissions will be accepted."*; transnet-shore-assistance-rfq: same).
- Pricing is a decoy trap: a paper "Section 4 Quotation Form" / priced schedule exists in the RFQ pack, but only the electronic price entered in the eSupplier portal counts (transnet-shore-assistance-rfq: *"Bidders note that all pricing must be completed in the eSupplier portal, electronic pricing. No paper pricing schedule shall be accepted."*; same wording in ocds-9t57fa-164264 and ocds-9t57fa-165835).
- No sealing/labeling instructions apply since there is no physical box — Not observed in sampled packs for any hard-copy channel.

## Municipal-arrears / rates clause

**Not observed in sampled packs.** Across all 9 corpus2 documents and the RFQ JSON, "municipal"/"arrears"/"rates" hits are limited to municipal permits/bylaws for site works (e.g. ocds-9t57fa-164264: *"the Contractor shall be responsible for obtaining all required municipal permits"*) and B-BBEE affidavit proof-of-address references (municipal/Eskom bill as proof of rural residence in ocds-9t57fa-165835). No clause requiring bidders/directors to be "not more than 90 days in municipal rates arrears" appears anywhere — this is a municipal-buyer feature that Transnet, as a national SOE, does not carry.

## B-BBEE treatment

**Points-only (80/20 or 90/10 preference-point system), not a hard pre-qualification gate**, in every RFQ/RFP sampled.

- Standard mechanics per transnet-shore-assistance-rfq: *"B-BBEE Status Level 1 or 2 = 20 points; Non-compliant and/or Level 3-8 = 0 points... Failure on the part of a bidder to submit proof of specific goals together with the bid will be interpreted to mean that preference points for B-BBEE status level of contribution are not claimed."* — i.e. missing B-BBEE proof costs points, it does not disqualify the bid.
- Threshold for which point system applies is Rand-value-based (ocds-9t57fa-164264: *"the 80/20 system for requirements with a Rand value of up to or equal to..."* [90/10 above threshold]).
- Fraudulent B-BBEE claims ARE a disqualification/penalty trigger (transnet-shore-assistance-rfq: *"If the B-BBEE status level of contributor has been claimed or obtained on a fraudulent basis... the purchaser may... disqualify the person from the bidding process."*).
- Evidence accepted: SANAS-accredited verification agency certificate, sworn affidavit (Commissioner of Oaths) for EME/QSE with ≥51% black ownership, or CIPC certificate for EME; JV/consortium must submit a consolidated scorecard (transnet-shore-assistance-rfq, ocds-9t57fa-164264).
- For long-term concessions (25-year Floating Dry Dock Facility Operator Agreement, ocds-9t57fa-165033), B-BBEE goes beyond a one-off scoring claim into **ongoing contractual commitment schedules**: "SCHEDULE 8A: B-BBEE Commitment," "SCHEDULE 8C: Black Ownership Commitment," "SCHEDULE 8D: Economic Development Plan," "SCHEDULE 8F: Economic Development Guidelines" — the operator must remain "a majority Black owned, BBBEE Level 1 company" as an ongoing contract condition, not merely a bid-stage points claim.
- No other Specific Goals (youth, disability, local content) are scored in the sampled RFQ pack, though subcontracting disclosure captures EME/QSE/black-ownership category for record purposes (transnet-shore-assistance-rfq).

## Cure/condonation policy

Transnet runs an explicit **three-tier document classification** that is consistent boilerplate across the RFQ-type packs (identical wording in transnet-shore-assistance-rfq and ocds-9t57fa-165835):

1. **Mandatory Returnable Documents** — no cure. *"Failure to provide all these Mandatory Returnable Documents at the Closing Date and time of this RFQ will result in a Respondent's disqualification."*
2. **Returnable Documents Used for Scoring** — no disqualification, but automatic zero on that criterion. *"Failure to provide all Returnable Documents used for purposes of scoring a bid, by the closing date and time of this bid will not result in a Respondent's disqualification. However, Bidders will receive an automatic score of zero for the applicable evaluation criterion."*
3. **Essential Returnable Documents** — curable once. *"Failure to provide essential Returnable Documents may result in Transnet affording Respondents a further opportunity to submit by a set deadline, where applicable. Should a Respondent thereafter fail to submit the requested documents, this may result in a Respondent's disqualification."*

Beyond documents, Transnet also allows a **cure-before-kill for unacceptable contractual deviations**: *"Respondents will be afforded an opportunity to withdraw an unacceptable deviation, failing which the respondent will be disqualified"* (transnet-shore-assistance-rfq) — but a *material* deviation from standard T&Cs "could result in disqualification" outright, so the cure window applies to non-material deviations only. Alterations to submitted prices are curable if initialled by the signatory but uncured alterations risk only that line item being excluded from award consideration, not the whole bid (transnet-shore-assistance-rfq).

## Security/vetting requirements

- **Post-award security clearance** to CONFIDENTIAL/SECRET/TOP SECRET level, applicable to the successful respondent, its personnel, and its subcontractors, obtained at the bidder's own cost/responsibility, is a standard clause (transnet-shore-assistance-rfq and ocds-9t57fa-165835, identical wording: *"Acceptance of this bid could be subject to the condition that the Successful Respondent, its personnel providing the goods and its subcontractor(s) must obtain security clearance from the appropriate authorities to the level of CONFIDENTIAL/SECRET/TOP SECRET. Obtaining the required clearance is the responsibility of the Successful Respondent."*) — given TNPA's critical-port-infrastructure remit this appears even in relatively low-value RFQs (welding spares, ocds-9t57fa-165835).
- **Service Provider Integrity Pact** is a standard returnable schedule across NEC3 RFPs (ocds-9t57fa-165125: "T2.2-13 Service Provider Integrity Pact"; ocds-9t57fa-165605: "T2.2-27"; ocds-9t57fa-165036: "T2.2-22") and RFQ packs ("Transnet's Supplier Integrity Pact," ocds-9t57fa-165835), and forms part of the RFQ Section 5 Certificate of Acquaintance in transnet-shore-assistance-rfq.
- **POPIA declaration** is a standalone standard returnable section — "Section 7"/"Section 8: Protection of Personal Information" — in both the RFQ pack (transnet-shore-assistance-rfq) and ocds-9t57fa-165835 (*"The Parties acknowledge and agree that, in relation to personal information that will be processed pursuant to [this agreement]... consent; data subject; electronic communication; information officer; operator; person; personal information..."*).
- **Former-employee / DPIP-FPPO disclosure** is distinctive: bidders must disclose any former Transnet employee or board member among owners/directors/shareholders going back **10 years**, and separately disclose Domestic Prominent Influential Persons/Foreign Prominent Public Officials (DPIP/FPPO) relationships, which Transnet is obliged to **publish annually on its website** (transnet-shore-assistance-rfq: *"must disclose any former Transnet employee/board member in owner/director/shareholder chain within past 10 years... Failure to furnish complete and accurate information in this regard will lead to the disqualification of a response..."*; ocds-9t57fa-165835: *"Respondents declaring a commercial relationship with a DPIP or FPPO are to note that Transnet is required to annually publish on its website a list of all business contracts entered into with DPIP or FPPO."*).
- **Fronting due diligence** on subcontractors is explicit: *"Transnet reserves the right to conduct due diligence assessments on the sub-contractor(s)... as well as conducting any necessary investigations on the sub-contractor(s) to detect issues of 'FRONTING'"* (ocds-9t57fa-165835).

## Financial demands

- **NEC3-standard insurance tables** (Contractor-provided) appear in every construction/term-service RFP: liability for death/injury of employees, motor vehicle liability with a stated minimum indemnity (ocds-9t57fa-164264: *"Motor Vehicle Liability Insurance comprising (as a minimum) 'Balance of Third Party' Risks including Passenger and Unauthorised Passenger Liability indemnity with a minimum indemnity limit of R5 000 000."*), and loss/damage to own property — costs are "deemed included in the tenderer's rates and prices" rather than separately reimbursed (ocds-9t57fa-165125, ocds-9t57fa-164264, ocds-9t57fa-165605).
- **Professional indemnity cover** required for design/detailing-type work, with the cover limit set by the Employer rather than fixed in the document (ocds-9t57fa-165036: *"it shall be the Contractor's responsibility to arrange professional indemnity cover through an insurance company acceptable to the Employer, the limits of such cover to be determined by the Employer in relation to the Service."*).
- **Advance/performance bank guarantees** are recoverable on default: *"Encash the advance bank guarantee and performance bond or warranty bond, if furnished by the Tenderer/Service Provider/Contractor, in order to recover the payments, already made by Transnet, along with interest"* (ocds-9t57fa-164264, ocds-9t57fa-165036, ocds-9t57fa-165605 — identical remedy clause).
- **CIDB grading certificate** (correct designated grading) is a mandatory returnable for construction-type RFPs (ocds-9t57fa-164264: *"A valid CIDB certificate in the correct designated grading"*; ocds-9t57fa-165036: dedicated T2.2-02 CIDB Grading Designation schedule).
- **Tax Compliance Status (TCS) PIN or CSD registration** is mandatory across all pack types, with each JV/consortium/subcontractor member required to submit its own separate certificate (transnet-shore-assistance-rfq: *"IN BIDS WHERE UNINCORPORATED CONSORTIA / JOINT VENTURES / SUB-CONTRACTORS ARE INVOLVED, EACH PARTY MUST SUBMIT A SEPARATE TCS CERTIFICATE / PIN / CSD NUMBER."*).
- **Letter of Good Standing with the Compensation Fund** required, with separate letters for each JV member (ocds-9t57fa-164264: *"Letter of Good Standing with the Workmen's Compensation Fund by the tendering entity or separate Letters of Good Standing from all members of a newly constituted JV."*).
- **Audited financials / bank ratings:** Not observed in sampled packs as an explicit line item (the sampled RFQs/RFPs rely on TCS/CSD/CIDB/Compensation-Fund proof rather than bank letters or credit ratings).

## Functionality norms

- Two-stage (RFQ) vs three-stage (RFP/construction) evaluation, depending on pack type.
  - RFQs (transnet-shore-assistance-rfq): **no separate functionality stage at all** — straight to Step 1 pass/fail responsiveness, then Step 2 Price(80)+B-BBEE(20) scoring, with an optional Step 3 sequential Post-Tender Negotiation (PTN) if the top price is not judged "market-related."
  - Construction/term-service RFPs (ocds-9t57fa-164264): explicit "Stage Three - Functionality" with a **60-point minimum qualifying threshold**, scored by not less than 3 evaluators independently (*"Functionality shall be scored independently by not less than 3 (three) evaluators"*), and failure removes the tender entirely: *"failure to meet the minimum threshold will result in the tender being disqualified and removed from any further consideration."* Only tenders that clear 60 proceed to the 80/20 or 90/10 preference-point system, with the system chosen by Rand-value threshold of the requirement.
  - Functionality criteria style: experience-based (e.g. "Previous Experience... within the past 10 years," supported by dated, signed reference letters/completion certificates on company letterhead) (ocds-9t57fa-164264).

## Distinctive kill rules / quirks

- **Sequential Post-Tender Negotiation (PTN) cascade**: if the top-ranked price is not "market-related," Transnet negotiates with #1, then #2, then #3 in order (not simultaneously); if none agree, the whole RFQ can be cancelled — meaning a firm-holding #1 bidder can lose the negotiation slot to #2 (transnet-shore-assistance-rfq winning_insights).
- **Punctuality trip-wire at compulsory briefings**: *"The Compulsory Tender Clarification Meeting will start punctually, and information will not be repeated for the benefit of Tenderers arriving late"* (ocds-9t57fa-165125, ocds-9t57fa-164264) — arriving even slightly late risks missing addenda-triggering information with no re-briefing, on top of the standard non-attendance disqualification.
- **Paper pricing-form decoy**: a "Section 4 Quotation Form"/priced schedule exists in the PDF pack purely as an acknowledgement page — actual pricing MUST be entered in the eSupplier electronic portal, and a bidder who prices only on the PDF risks being found non-responsive for lacking "a priced offer" (transnet-shore-assistance-rfq).
- **Open-ended bid validity for the eventual winner**: once the adjudication body approves an award, "the validity of the successful bidder(s)' bid will be deemed to remain valid until a final contract has been concluded" — meaning an unsuccessful #2/#3 can remain contractually "on the hook" at their quoted price even after being told they lost, until the process fully concludes (transnet-shore-assistance-rfq).
- **"Notice and Comment" non-competitive lease bypass**: TNPA can skip open tendering for property leases and instead run a public objection window under its internal Lease Management Manual §7.5 where premises are landlocked or access-constrained to a single party — *"a notice and comments process may be followed if there are land-locked premises, constraint, or limited access to one specific party... to mitigate the risk to operational continuity"* (ocds-9t57fa-164857) — a distinctive SOE self-exemption mechanism not seen as a formal, published carve-out in the other sampled packs.
- **10-year former-employee lookback + annual DPIP/FPPO public disclosure**: uniquely long disclosure window (most SOE conflict-of-interest clauses look back 12 months) combined with a standing obligation on Transnet itself to publish a public list of contracts with politically-exposed persons annually (transnet-shore-assistance-rfq, ocds-9t57fa-165835).
- **Undisclosed-subcontracting penalty is a fixed percentage, not automatic disqualification**: *"if the successful bidder subcontracted a portion of the bid to another person without disclosing it, Transnet reserves the right to penalise the bidder up to 10 percent of the value of the contract"* (transnet-shore-assistance-rfq) — a contract-value clawback rather than a bid-stage kill.
- **Long-term concessions convert B-BBEE from a scoring claim into a running contractual obligation**: the 25-year Floating Dry Dock Facility Operator Agreement embeds standing Black Ownership Commitment and Economic Development Plan schedules the operator must maintain for the life of the contract, not just prove at bid stage (ocds-9t57fa-165033).
